clue.text: Catching cold, remedy immediately

indicators.note: one word catching another holds it inside, so the remedy word surrounds the cold abbreviation

parts.note: to atone is to make amends, to remedy a wrong
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Advice to treat a chill straight away before it worsens.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside ATONE to give AT ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean without any delay, straight away, right now.

clue.text: Going round Dubai? Bah! It's along the coast

indicators.note: letters going round are spun about and come out in a different order

parts.note: the letters of the city name and the exclamation together

explanation.surface: A grumpy tourist circling Dubai, dismissing it, and pointing out somewhere else further along the shore.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cheekily relative to Dubai: Abu Dhabi lies along the same Gulf coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is the Emirati capital, a city sitting a short drive further down the Gulf shoreline from Dubai.

clue.text: May, perhaps: leader deposed by party taken in by exotic creature? Exactly

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it, so the party sits within the creature
deposing the leader removes whoever stands at the front, so the first letter goes

parts.note: May is an example of a month of the year
ET, the extra-terrestrial, is an alien being
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Theresa May ousted by a party, as though swallowed by some strange beast: political satire.
explanation.walkthrough: May looks like the former Prime Minister, but she is just a month. ONTH + E(DO)T gives ON THE DOT.
explanation.definitionFit: On the dot means precisely, punctually, with no deviation from the stated time.

clue.text: Left, in bed, a little horse

indicators.note: placed in something means put inside it, so the letter goes within the bed word

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A small pony left lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A colt is a young male horse, so a small, immature equine fits.

clue.text: Delivery with keeper initially missing, run yielded, cricket's shameful, concerning

indicators.note: a shameful performance is a mess, so the surviving letters are jumbled
something missing is absent, so that letter is removed from the cricket word
what is yielded is given up, so the run letter is surrendered too

parts.note: the word with its S, as printed

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the keeper word

parts.note: first letter of keeper
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
on means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A cricket report: a ball bowled, the wicketkeeper absent, runs conceded, the whole display a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: Delivery looks like a cricket ball but means childbirth; K and R are the standard keeper and run letters removed before the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A C-section, or Caesarean section, is a surgical method of birth, so a delivery of a baby.

clue.text: Devil turns ego fluently — being this?

definitions.text: Devil turns ego fluently — being this?

indicators.note: fluently suggests letters flowing freely and settling in a new order

parts.note: all three words supply the letters

explanation.surface: The Devil smoothly redirects someone's vanity, being a persuasive talker.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: the Devil, famously persuasive, would be silver-tongued as he works on a person's pride.
explanation.definitionFit: Silver-tongued describes someone eloquent and persuasive, a smooth talker like the tempter of legend.

clue.text: Gloats over achievement loudly, part of old Boat Race

parts.note: to crow is to boast or gloat

indicators.note: said loudly means spoken out, so we go by how the achievement word sounds

parts.note: a feat is an achievement

explanation.surface: Rowers bragging noisily about their win in the historic Oxford–Cambridge Boat Race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race looks like the Oxford v Cambridge rowing contest, but in Cockney rhyming slang boat race means face.
explanation.definitionFit: Crow's feet are the wrinkles at the corners of the eyes, part of an aged person's face.

clue.text: Twice I see in France the frosty figure

parts.note: I and C (sounds like see) written two times
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A traveller twice spotting the same snowman in France.
explanation.walkthrough: C stands for see by sound, a common crossword shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: An icicle is a hanging spike of frozen water, a shape formed by frost.

clue.text: Deny most of teenage mucking about

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its final letter
mucking about is messing around, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: teenage without its final E

explanation.surface: Denying that most of the adolescent horseplay happened.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate is to contradict or refuse to accept, as a synonym of reject.

clue.text: To the point that peacekeepers fired back

parts.note: the United Nations sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: going back runs in the opposite direction, so the fired word is read right to left

parts.note: lit as in set alight

explanation.surface: Troops held fire up to the moment that they were shot at, then returned it.
explanation.definitionFit: Until means up to the time or degree that something happens.

clue.text: Whupping good, replacing starter, moving fast

indicators.note: replacing the starter swaps out the opening letter for a new one

parts.note: a walloping is a thrashing
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A satisfying beating, and someone racing away.
explanation.walkthrough: G takes the place of the W at the start of WALLOPING.
explanation.definitionFit: Galloping is a horse's fastest gait, so it means travelling at great speed.

clue.text: Good angle, taking in ancient game where all can see

indicators.note: taking something in means enclosing it, so the ancient word goes inside

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
ancient means old
to angle is to fish with a rod
bowls is a game played on a green

explanation.surface: A pleasing camera angle on a historic sporting contest, broadcast to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: Angle is the verb meaning to go fishing, not a geometric angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Goldfish bowls are idiomatically places or situations with no privacy, exposed to everyone's view.

clue.text: German philosopher, no-good rotter

indicators.note: no here says the following item is absent from the philosopher's name

parts.note: Georg Hegel, the German idealist philosopher
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a German thinker as a worthless scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: No-good reads as one insult but splits into no plus G.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel is informal for a contemptible, untrustworthy man, a cad.

clue.text: Hint describing piece of language?

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so one word goes around another

parts.note: a cue is a prompt or hint

indicators.note: a piece of a word is just a bit of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of language

explanation.surface: A self-describing riddle: a pointer that explains a bit of wording.
explanation.walkthrough: Describing means drawing round, so CUE goes around L. The whole clue doubles as a description of a crossword clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword clue is a hint written in words that points to a particular word.

clue.text: Break in Adriatic city

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to crack or divide
second meaning: a port city on the Croatian coast

explanation.surface: A holiday break on the Adriatic coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is both a verb for cracking apart and the name of Croatia's second city on the Dalmatian shore.

clue.text: Primarily, big English opus wherein Unferð loses face?

definitions.text: Primarily, big English opus wherein Unferð loses face?

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the opening letter of each following word

parts.words: big English opus wherein Unferð loses face
parts.note: the leading letters of the seven words

explanation.surface: A grand Old English epic in which the warrior Unferð is humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: In the poem Unferð taunts the hero and is shamed by his reply; the whole clue describes the poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Beowulf is the great Old English heroic poem, a major early work of English literature featuring Unferð.

clue.text: Not popular with crackers, Devon Blue

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters following go wild into a new order

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A Devon blue cheese that nobody wants with their crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: Crackers looks like the biscuits served with cheese, but it signals the anagram. Devon Blue is an English blue cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbeloved means not cherished or liked, so unpopular.

clue.text: Clothing essential at golf course

definitions.note: the things found at a golf course
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the pegs or starting areas on each hole

explanation.surface: A dress code note about what must be worn at the golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: Tees are casual T-shirts, a wardrobe staple, and also the pegs and starting spots on golf holes.

clue.text: Maid of honour eating words at wedding

indicators.note: the phrase eating something has it swallowed inside, spanning the word gap

parts.note: found across the end of maid and the start of of

explanation.surface: A bridesmaid tucking into the reception food.
explanation.definitionFit: The bride and groom each say these vows when accepting marriage at the ceremony.

clue.text: I almost tolerate most of nonsense somewhere in Turkey

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written
to stand something is to tolerate it

indicators.note: most of means all but the end, so the last letter goes again

parts.note: bull is slang for nonsense

explanation.surface: A traveller who can barely put up with the rubbish talked at a Turkish destination.
explanation.definitionFit: Istanbul is Turkey's largest city, a place within the country.

clue.text: Alas, today's as dismal

indicators.note: something dismal is in a poor state, so the letters end up badly arranged

parts.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A sigh that the present day is gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas and sad to say are both expressions of regret introducing unwelcome news.

clue.text: Painful condition overwhelming one bird

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the condition wraps around the one

parts.note: IBS is irritable bowel syndrome
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sick bird laid low by an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: The ibis is a long-legged wading bird with a curved bill.

clue.text: Some frown at a shampoo being depicted in War and Peace

definitions.text: being depicted in War and Peace

indicators.note: some of the phrase means just a portion of the run of letters

parts.note: running from the end of frown into shampoo

explanation.surface: Someone scowling at a hair product shown in Tolstoy's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Natasha Rostova is a leading character portrayed in Tolstoy's epic novel.

clue.text: Fuss when two of hearts switched for diamonds with gizmo

indicators.note: switched for means exchanged, one card suit traded for another

parts.note: a hoo-hah is a commotion or fuss
H is the card abbreviation for hearts, and both occurrences are meant
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A card player grumbling over a swap of suits, using some device.
explanation.walkthrough: Both H's in HOOHAH become D's.
explanation.definitionFit: A doodah is informal for a thingamajig whose name escapes you, much like a gadget.

clue.text: Rudolf, the German behind something energising locomotives to begin with?

parts.note: die is a German word for the

indicators.note: to begin with points to the first letter of each of the following words

parts.note: the leading letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Rudolf Diesel, the German inventor of the engine that powers trains.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true: Rudolf Diesel invented the diesel engine used in locomotives.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf was the first name of the engineer Diesel, so the surname completes his name.

clue.text: Window concealed by signori elusively

indicators.note: concealed by means tucked away inside the words that follow

parts.note: running from the end of signori into elusively

explanation.surface: Italian gentlemen slyly hiding behind a window.
explanation.definitionFit: An oriel is a bay window projecting from an upper storey.

clue.text: Being overheard, piped down

indicators.note: overheard means caught by ear, so the sound of the next word counts

parts.note: piped as in played a wind instrument, blew

explanation.surface: Someone caught eavesdropping is told to pipe down and hush.
explanation.walkthrough: Piped down reads as a phrase meaning be quiet, but the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling blue and feeling down both mean low-spirited or sad.

clue.text: German philosopher's hypocrisy called out

indicators.note: something called out is spoken aloud, so its sound gives the letters

parts.note: cant is hypocritical, sanctimonious talk

explanation.surface: A German thinker's double standards are publicly exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: Called out looks like exposing the hypocrisy, but it marks the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Immanuel Kant was the eighteenth-century Prussian thinker behind the Critique of Pure Reason.

clue.text: Copy of doohickey regularly backfiring

indicators.note: backfiring sends things the wrong way, so the letters run backwards
regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A replica gadget that misfires.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a repetition or imitation of something, a reproduction of an original.

clue.text: Denied visa, we'd do in resort

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort means sorting again into a fresh order

parts.note: the letters of all three words

explanation.surface: A traveller refused a visa, planning to have the wedding at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Resort looks like a holiday spot but is read as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Disavowed means repudiated or refused to acknowledge, so rejected as untrue.

clue.text: Servant comes before some French king, wanting support

parts.note: a help is a domestic servant
des is French for some
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A servant takes precedence over a French monarch who lacks backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A help desk is the service providing technical assistance to users, so support by another name.

clue.text: Type of tennis shot: very weak-spirited, coming up short

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very

indicators.note: coming up suggests rising the opposite way, so the letters run backwards
short means lacking its end, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: yellow means cowardly

explanation.surface: A tennis stroke played timidly that falls short of the net.
explanation.walkthrough: Yellow is informal for cowardly, hence weak-spirited; in an across clue, coming up still serves as a backwards signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A volley is a tennis stroke hitting the ball before it bounces.
